I've been working this land in Quzhou my whole life. Forty-five years tells you what to do without much thinking. My wheat-maize plots and my cotton plots are separate — the rotation runs on the bigger piece, cotton gets the rest.

My boy and second daughter are working in Baoding now, so it's mostly me and my wife managing the farm, with the others coming back for busy season. That means I can't overwork the land with too many operations. I keep things simple but I don't cut corners on what matters — water and fertilizer at the right times.

For wheat, I'll use the improved Jimai variety that's been reliable here. Three irrigations — before freezing, jointing, and heading. I learned the hard way that skipping the jointing water kills yield. Two pesticide runs: one herbicide pass early, one aphid and mildew treatment at heading.

For maize I always buy hybrid seed —郑单958 or whatever the seed station is pushing this year that's proven. I direct-seed into the wheat stubble, no ploughing. My back isn't what it was and it saves diesel money. Two irrigations if it's a dry summer.

Cotton is the headache crop. More work, more sprays — bollworm doesn't forgive you. But prices have been okay and I know how to grow it. I'll plough before planting. Four irrigations, five pesticide applications minimum.
